sentence: This project studies how small molecules switch on voltage-dependent potassium channels and searches for potassium channel openers.
This project studies how environmental agents affect the stress response and how changes to RNA modifications lead to cancer.
This project studies how harmful gene mutations cause motor neuron degeneration and which biological pathways are disturbed in patient neurons.
This project studies how the tumor inflammasome contributes to harmful side effects of antibody immunotherapy in cancer patients.
This project provides biobanking, histology and molecular testing services that support basic and translational research and clinical trials.
This project builds an imaging system that uses photon-counting detectors and algorithms to show very small vessels more clearly despite motion and noise.
This project builds a system that gathers imaging, radiotherapy and clinical data and makes the data easy to share.
This project provides tissue collection, pathology review and advanced analysis of lymphoma specimens to support research projects.
This project studies how a neutrophil protein helps peptides stop neutrophils forming DNA-based traps and whether this affects survival of infected newborn mice.
This project studies the gamete fusion machinery of the malaria parasite and tests whether it could be a target for transmission blocking vaccines.
This project tests whether removing or blocking an upstream open reading frame raises the amount of protein a gene linked to epilepsy makes in neurons.
This project studies how a transcription factor in the habenula controls nicotine intake.
This project uses an equine parvovirus that infects the liver to study how DNA damage response pathways affect viral genome replication and viral hepatitis.
This project studies how social determinants of health affect the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
This project studies how systemic autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus lead to blood problems such as anemia.
This project tries to find out whether amyloidosis is already present in carriers of a gene allele who have no symptoms.
This project studies how protein kinases work at the molecular level in the signaling pathways that control cell fate or number.
This project develops therapies and cell therapies for children with cancer and studies the molecular mechanisms of childhood cancers.
This project studies how myeloid cells weaken T cells in hepatocellular carcinoma and how liver disease and immunotherapy affect these cells.
